- The 2019 Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) are a national deprivation measure released by the Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government (MHCLG).  
- IMD 2019 comprises seven core domains with the following weightings:  
  * Income Deprivation – 22.5%  
  * Employment Deprivation – 22.5%  
  * Education, Skills and Training Deprivation – 13.5%  
  * Health Deprivation and Disability – 13.5%  
  * Crime – 9.3%  
  * Barriers to Housing and Services – 9.3%  
  * Living Environment Deprivation – 9.3%  
- The Income Deprivation Domain is defined as the proportion of the population experiencing deprivation related to low income, encompassing both those out‑of‑work and those in work with low earnings who meet the means‑test thresholds.  
- A domain score is interpretable as a percentage: e.g., a score of 0.38 on the Income Deprivation Domain reflects 38 % of the population being income‑deprived.  
- Two supplementary indices report income deprivation among specific age groups:  
  * Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index (IDACI) – proportion of children aged 0‑15 in income‑deprived families.  
  * Income Deprivation Affecting Older People Index (IDAOPI) – proportion of residents aged 60+ experiencing income deprivation.
